qa.user_verbatim_complaint: Fix the previously introduced recovery debts so manually restored Happy sessions are not misleadingly treated as durable daemon state, user-stopped/archived sessions are not resurrected, restore-in-progress does not trigger false recovery, and OOM protection targets runaway session process groups instead of taking down the server.
qa.overall_assessment: Static inspection and a redirected dry-run verify most low-level guard/recovery mechanics landed, but QA objects to closing the cycle because the implementation still lacks the architect-required daemon-owned spawn/adoption path and does not wire manual stop/archive flows to create tombstones. Those gaps leave the deeper recovery debt unresolved even though reporting now avoids overclaiming daemon tracking.

constraints_observed.dry_run_notes: Guard dry-run was executed from a temporary copy with LOCK/DANGER/ACTION/LOG paths redirected to /tmp/qa-guard-20260523-235421.vqp8jq and HAPPY_GUARD_DRY_RUN=1; production services/sessions were not stopped or killed.

objections.issue: Daemon-owned spawn/adoption remains unimplemented; recovery still uses external systemd-run/direct spawns and hard-codes daemon_tracked_restored=0.
evidence: daemon_spawn_session uses systemd-run for happy-session-* transient units rather than the daemon control spawn path (/root/bin/happy-session-recovery.sh:1167-1191).
Success log is explicitly 'Externally spawned (non-daemon-tracked until daemon adopts it)' (/root/bin/happy-session-recovery.sh:1235).
Bulk restore logs external_restored and daemon_tracked_restored=0 (/root/bin/happy-session-recovery.sh:1518).
Manual recover says daemon adoption must be verified separately (/root/bin/happy-session-recovery.sh:1795-1797).
Static grep found no /spawn-session, /session-started adoption call, or daemon-owned restore API in the recovery script.
objections.why_blocks: The architect finding says daemon-owned spawn/adoption is the deeper requirement. Truthful labeling is an improvement, but it is not a durable daemon-owned restore and therefore does not clean up the core tracking debt.
objections.recommendation: Implement restore through the live daemon's spawn/adoption mechanism, or add an explicit adoption verification step that proves restored PIDs enter pidToTrackedSession and are present in daemon snapshots before counting them as recovered.

objections.issue: Tombstone storage and restore filtering exist, but normal manual stop/archive workflows are not wired to create tombstones, so user-stopped/archived sessions can still be resurrected unless an operator manually runs a new tombstone command.
evidence: Recovery defines per-home tombstone files and CLI tombstone/untombstone commands (/root/bin/happy-session-recovery.sh:818-865,2143-2165).
Restore filters tombstoned sessions before spawn and checks tombstones per session (/root/bin/happy-session-recovery.sh:1403-1414,1443-1446).
Repository-wide grep found tombstone references only in /root/bin/happy-session-recovery.sh, not in daemon stop-session or app/archive paths.
Dev report recommendation explicitly says to wire manual stop/archive workflows to call the new tombstone command, proving this binding lifecycle integration is not done.
objections.why_blocks: The ticket goal is that user-stopped/archived sessions are not resurrected. A skip list that recovery respects is necessary but insufficient unless user stop/archive intent is durably recorded at the point of action.
objections.recommendation: Update the actual stop-session/archive code path to write the tombstone for the correct Happy home/session before or atomically with the user action; then verify restore skips those entries without operator side steps.

acceptance_results.verification_method: Static control-flow inspection of watch_sessions fast-detect handling.
acceptance_results.evidence: /root/bin/happy-session-recovery.sh:730-739 aborts fast-detect when the process-list hash stabilizes; /root/bin/happy-session-recovery.sh:782-786 also aborts when removals stop.

acceptance_results.criterion: Runtime watcher never uses peak snapshot merely because current saved count is below peak; peak snapshots are only for cold boot/disaster mode.
acceptance_results.verification_method: Static inspection of peak protection and restore source selection.
acceptance_results.evidence: /root/bin/happy-session-recovery.sh:500-528 preserves the desired session_dirs.txt on runtime drops and writes only JSON history; /root/bin/happy-session-recovery.sh:1382-1399 reads peak JSON only when session_dirs.txt is empty and HAPPY_RECOVERY_DISASTER_MODE=1.

acceptance_results.criterion: Recovery respects a durable tombstone/skip list for manually stopped or archived sessions.
acceptance_results.verification_method: Static inspection plus repository grep for tombstone integration points.

acceptance_results.criterion: Recovery report distinguishes daemon-tracked restore from external/non-daemon restore and does not overclaim.
acceptance_results.verification_method: Static inspection of restore counters and manual recover messaging.

acceptance_results.verification_method: Static inspection plus redirected dry-run candidate scan.

acceptance_results.criterion: No change imposes a coarse memory limit on the whole happy daemon.

build_verification.skip_reason: Operational shell and systemd-unit changes only; user explicitly constrained QA to static inspection and safe dry-run, with no service restart/reload.

hardcode_scan_results.notes: Operational scripts intentionally contain fixed Happy home/service paths from the documented host topology; QA did not treat those as new portability violations for this cycle.

all_findings.issue: Core daemon-owned spawn/adoption requirement remains unresolved; restored sessions are still external and not proven daemon-tracked.
all_findings.recommendation: Restore through daemon-owned spawn/adoption and verify pidToTrackedSession/snapshot membership before counting a session as recovered.

all_findings.issue: Tombstone support is not wired to normal manual stop/archive intent creation.
all_findings.recommendation: Write tombstones from the stop/archive workflows for the correct home/session, then keep the existing restore-side skip checks.

critical_issues: Restores are still external systemd-run/direct spawns and not daemon-owned/adoption-verified.
Tombstone records are not generated by normal manual stop/archive workflows.
refined_context.recommended_approach: Move recovery spawning/adoption into daemon-owned control flow or prove adoption into pidToTrackedSession before counting recovery; wire stop/archive actions to create per-home tombstones before restore can resurrect them.
refined_context.additional_context: Keep existing passing fixes: stable fast-detect abort, disaster-only peak use, restore lock suppression, truthful external reporting, Codex preservation, and targeted OOM guard dry-run behavior.
